site.name: Dzmitryi Kharlanau — SAP Knowledge, Practical Lab & Technology Watch

objective.primary: Make the public workspace unambiguous to search systems and AI agents: keep employer and client context private, route durable questions to the Knowledge Base, route executable tasks to the Practical Lab, and route fast-moving developments to Technology Watch. Do not infer independent commercial services.
targetQuestions: What public SAP knowledge is available for learning, interviews, assessments and technical decisions?
Which reviewed and indexable sources can support a factual SAP answer?
Which practical setup or tool can help with a difficult enterprise-engineering task?
What new SAP, enterprise AI, integration, data or engineering development is worth tracking?
What information is intentionally private and outside the public site?
Which machine-readable interfaces, datasets, Agent Skills and MCP packages expose the public knowledge?
What crawler, reuse, evidence and correction policies apply to the public material?
canonicalTerms: Senior SAP Consultant at EPAM Systems

entityHome.notes: The homepage exposes four public routes: Private boundary, Knowledge Base, Practical Setup, and Technology Watch.

siteProfile.notes: ARWP site profile declares the public-workspace routing extension and points to /ai/focus-map.json.

llmsCanonical.notes: The manifest states the non-commercial professional boundary and four public routes before the deeper knowledge model.

answerPages.description: Use the focus map first. Route durable factual or learning questions to reviewed Knowledge/Labs sources, executable engineering tasks to the Practical Lab, and current-change questions to Technology Watch. Preserve review and index state; never route to a legacy service URL as a commercial offer.

originalResearch.description: Publish bounded experiments, datasets and source-backed analyses as public evidence with explicit review state and limitations.

protocolObservatory.description: Add a dated source-backed observatory only if agentic-web protocol tracking becomes a recurring subject of this professional site rather than duplicating the dedicated ARWP project.

comparisonPages.description: Add comparison pages where recurring SAP, integration, data or AI decisions benefit from stable side-by-side trade-offs and evidence.

conceptDefinitions.description: Use reviewed Atlas glossary and canonical entity pages for stable definitions after the public task route is known.

claimsRegistry.description: Introduce stable claim identifiers only for high-value professional or technical assertions that need explicit evidence, review date and supersession history.

evidenceReceipts.description: Add replayable evidence receipts for selected generated or evaluated artifacts when exact input, output and provenance materially improve trust.

crawlerMatrix.description: Publish a dated machine-readable view of the site's explicit robots policy, separating search and user-directed retrieval from model-training crawler access.

agentFetchLab.description: Measure whether agents correctly separate public knowledge, practical tasks, technology research and private professional context.

knowledgeGraph.description: Maintain a canonical JSON-LD graph connecting person identity, the website and the site's public machine-readable discovery and trust surfaces.

citationVisuals.description: Publish reusable diagrams with stable URLs, source notes and explicit reuse terms where visuals materially improve public technical understanding.

openReuseAssets.description: Create a dedicated media and reuse-rights surface only when reusable public diagrams, learning assets or research artifacts warrant a separate permission model.

trustCenter.description: Publish one canonical trust surface covering identity, review model, citation, security reporting, crawler policy, corrections and evidence boundaries for both primary directions.

correctionsLedger.description: Maintain a public machine-readable ledger for material corrections instead of silently changing important published factual claims.

softwareProvenance.description: The website is not represented as a released software package; repository history and CI provide source history, but no package-level provenance or security attestation is claimed.

persistentIdentifiers.description: Use DOI or another externally issued persistent identifier only for datasets or research artifacts where durable citation value justifies it, and never claim one before issuance.

externalTrustSignals.description: Expose independent trust signals only when an external source actually exists and its scope can be stated without turning it into a correctness or expertise certificate.

externalDistribution.description: Distribute selected substantial public knowledge externally while preserving this site as the canonical source of record.

aiVisibility.description: Measure discovery for Knowledge, Practical Lab, Technology Watch and professional-profile queries separately. Do not treat traffic to legacy service URLs as a commercial funnel.

localization.description: Keep English as the canonical public and machine language unless reviewed localization is explicitly reintroduced.

history.description: Expose a concise machine-readable site evolution timeline if product and knowledge-surface maturity becomes useful context for readers and agents.

vocabulary.definition: The site has four primary public routes: Private boundary, Knowledge Base, Practical Setup, and Technology Watch. Profile, Labs, Frameworks and Machine are supporting surfaces. Legacy service URLs are compatibility references only.

After a primary route is selected, the preferred knowledge chain establishes the enterprise domain, selects a reviewed decision, inspects an applied scenario and follows the claim back to reviewed evidence.

A site publication state indicating that content has passed the site's review and indexing rules and is allowed into public retrieval surfaces; structural completeness or inclusion in a navigation hub alone does not imply this state.

signals.name: public-workspace search visibility
signals.description: Track impressions, queries and landing-page performance separately for SAP learning/assessment intent and SAP AMS-optimization intent without claiming causal ranking gains.

signals.name: AI route accuracy
signals.description: Sample observable AI citations and referrals to check whether learning requests reach learning evidence and live operational problems reach AMS evidence.

signals.name: referring domains
signals.description: Track external sources that cite or link to reviewed learning, AMS, datasets and professional evidence.

measurement.privacy: Use aggregate and privacy-minimized visibility signals; do not create visitor-level browsing histories or infer private user intent from retrieval telemetry.
